title: finding(process): this shift's later claim comments were composed rather than copied from the template, so no `Claim:` first line exists — and the sanctioned `Clause-②-correction:` repair cannot attach to a claim with no id
body:
Filed **bare** by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`, session `session_011QreXiyMEqKLN4U5daMPVa`) — no labels, no type, no priority. Routing and grading are triage's output alone.

⭐ **This is a self-report of the filing seat's own defect**, filed because it is reproducible, it is already blocking two pull requests, and the sanctioned repair path provably cannot fix it.

## What happened

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` 〈模板与表〉 requires the claim comment in a **fixed shape whose first line is literally `Claim:`**, carrying `Session:`, `Branch:`, `Domain:`, `Clause-②: yes | no`, `Thread-read:` and the rest as their own lines.

This seat **composed** claims as markdown prose instead — `## Claim — \`domain:ui\` seat (\`os-tesla\`)` with the declaration written as `**Clause-②: yes.**`, bolded and with prose trailing on the same line.

⚠️ **It is a DRIFT WITHIN ONE SHIFT, not a standing repo condition** — measured, because the distinction decides who owns the repair:

| card | comments whose first line is literally `Claim:` |
|:--|--:|
| objectui#7386 (earlier, same shift) | **1** ✓ |
| objectui#9342 / objectui#9414 / objectui#9336 (later, same shift) | **0** ⛔ |

The template was followed early and abandoned later. ⛔ Nothing in the loop caught the drift — not the claim write, not the mandatory read-back (the text posted was exactly the text composed; it was the *shape* that was wrong), and not the race re-read.

## Why the sanctioned repair cannot clear it

`check-clause2-carriers --pair 9443` and `--pair 9442` both read **exit 4**, and its remedy is to post a `Clause-②-correction:` comment naming *"the numeric id of the claim comment it corrects"*. That was done on all three cards. The checker then reported, in its own words:

> A correction comment WAS posted and did NOT take effect: … it names a comment that is NOT this card's governing claim … **The governing claim comment carries no id in this reading, so no correction can be matched to it — that is a gap in the reading, not a defect in the correction.**

⇒ The correction mechanism presupposes a governing claim the reader can find. When the claim was never in the fixed shape, **there is none to name**, so the documented repair is unreachable by construction. ⭐ The checker says so itself rather than failing silently, which is the only reason this was caught at all.

## The open question — ⛔ NOT decided by this seat

The obvious repair is to post one properly-shaped `Claim:` comment on each affected card. The checker's remedy text says **⛔ a second `Claim:` is forbidden by the claim protocol**.

Whether that prohibition binds here turns on a real ambiguity this seat ⛔ will not resolve on its own authority:

- **Reading A — it does not bind.** "A *second* `Claim:`" presupposes a first, and there is none: the checker itself cannot find a governing claim. Ownership is not in question either (labels and assignee were set atomically and race-re-read at claim time, and this seat is the sole assignee), so the hazard the rule guards against — two competing claims — cannot arise.
- **Reading B — it binds as written.** The prohibition is unqualified and ⛔-marked, and a seat that reasons its way past a ⛔ on its own judgement is the failure mode the marks exist to prevent.

⚠️ Nothing is lost while this is undecided: CI on both pull requests is still converging, so neither could land yet regardless.

## What would stop it recurring

The checker already names the cause in its own text — *"every one of the five misses measured in the filing shift was a line composed from memory"*. This is the sixth, by the same cause, and the countermeasure it prescribes is **copy the template's line, never compose it**. A claim-shape check at write time (first line literally `Claim:`, the fixed lines present) would have caught all six at the moment of writing rather than at the enqueue gate, several hours and three cards later.

## Affected right now

objectui#9342 / PR objectui#9443 (`Clause-②: yes`, `needs:contract-review` on both carriers) · objectui#9414 / PR objectui#9442 (`Clause-②` overturned to `no` on published contract text) · objectui#9336 (`Clause-②: no`; PR not yet open).

⛔ No pull request is being enqueued past a red mechanical limb while this stands.
